evidence.title: Development and Assessment of an Artificial Intelligence-Based Tool for Ptosis Measurement in Adult Myasthenia Gravis Patients Using Selfie Video Clips Recorded on Smartphones
evidence.outcome: MRD1 estimation performance with versus without gating out poor-quality images
evidence.effect: Gating the test data to exclude poor-quality images did not improve model performance. Full test fold (N=664): r=0.732, MAE 0.822 mm.
evidence.quote: Model performance showed no improvement when test data were gated to exclude "poor" quality images.

evidence.title: DeepQuality improves infant retinopathy screening
evidence.outcome: Poor-quality image input detection
evidence.effect: Quality-defect detection for integrity, illumination, and clarity had AUCs ranging from 0.933 to 0.995.
evidence.quote: DeepQuality can accurately detect various quality defects concerning integrity, illumination, and clarity with area under the curve (AUC) values ranging from 0.933 to 0.995.

evidence.title: The need for guardrails with large language models in pharmacovigilance and other medical safety critical settings
evidence.outcome: Document-level uncertainty detecting non-ICSR/anomalous documents before LLM processing
evidence.effect: AUROC of 0.80 discriminating extraneous documents from validation ICSRs; not completely separated, three counterexamples.
evidence.quote: Although not completely separated, the separation of the validation and extraneous samples corresponds to an AUROC in the validation data of 0.80.
evidence.sample_unit: Japanese individual case safety reports (ICSRs) translated to English and reviewed by experts

evidence.title: Retinograd-AI: An Open-Source Automated Fundus Autofluorescence Retinal Image Gradability Assessment for Inherited Retinal Diseases
evidence.outcome: Gene prediction classifier accuracy with vs without image-quality filtering
evidence.effect: Filtering images with Retinograd-AI raised gene prediction classifier accuracy from 33.8% to 68.9%.
evidence.quote: Applying Retinograd-AI to filter images improved the accuracy of a gene prediction classifier from 33.8% to 68.9%.

evidence.title: Fact-Checking Large Language Model Responses to a Health Care Prompt: Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: elicitation of missing medication details
evidence.effect: GPT-4o asked for acne medication details; OpenBioLLM-70B did not, despite a shorter 75-word response versus 279 words.
evidence.quote: However, OpenBioLLM-70B did not mention the risk of acne medication during pregnancy and did not ask the patient to provide more information on her medication.
evidence.sample_unit: clinical claims (plus one acne scenario with 16 expert-identified claims)

evidence.title: Mind the Ambiguity: Aleatoric Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs for Safe Medical Question Answering
evidence.outcome: Medical QA accuracy with ambiguity detection and clarification requests versus baselines
evidence.effect: AU-Probe flags ambiguous input from hidden states and prompts the user to clarify; average accuracy improved 9.48% over baselines across four open LLMs.
evidence.quote: Extensive experiments across four open LLMs demonstrate the effectiveness of our QA framework, with an average accuracy improvement of 9.48% over baselines.

evidence.title: A knowledge-guided agentic framework for mitigating patient-context ambiguity in health queries
evidence.outcome: Diagnosis retrieval accuracy with vs without acquiring missing patient context before answering
evidence.effect: Framework increased exact Top-1 accuracy by at least 57.1 percentage points and selective exact Recall@5 by at least 77.7 points across five models versus direct prompting.
evidence.quote: In diagnosis retrieval, it increased overall exact Top-1 accuracy by at least 57.1 percentage points and selective exact Recall@5 by at least 77.7 percentage points across the five evaluated models compared with direct prompting.
evidence.sample_unit: queries (1,034 symptom queries plus 487 dietary-safety queries)

evidence.title: A decision-basis contract for auditable LLM-assisted medical billing verification: deterministic rules, verbatim evidence, and fail-closed abstention
evidence.outcome: Missing information identification
evidence.effect: Explicit documentation requirements improved identification of missing information for all four models.
evidence.quote: Explicit documentation requirements improved identification of missing information for all four models.

evidence.title: A clinic-updated digital twin for Parkinson’s disease progression: Governed Bayesian forecasting with uncertainty-gated reporting
evidence.outcome: Share of forecasts released or suppressed by confidence gate and reasons for suppression
evidence.effect: Gate released forecasts at 32.7% of visits (strict) and 48.1% (partial-observation extension); suppression driven by incomplete assessment (51.5%) rather than model uncertainty (0.2%).
evidence.quote: The confidence gate released governed forecasts at 32.7% of visits under strict three-domain requirements, increasing to 48.1% under a validated partial-observation extension.

evidence.title: Task-Specific Quality Gating for Retinal Optical Coherence Tomography B-Scans: Learned Representations Over Scalar Metrics in Choroid Segmentation
evidence.outcome: Task-specific OCT input quality gating
evidence.effect: ImageNet-based pretrained representations improved upon NR-IQA, achieving ROC-AUC up to 0.77.
evidence.quote: General-purpose ImageNet-based pretrained representations (EfficientNet-b0, ResNet-50, ViT-B/16) improve upon NR-IQA, achieving ROC-AUC up to 0.77, indicating that learned representations are better suited to task-specific quality gating than hand-crafted scalar statistics.

evidence.title: DeepMonitoring: a deep learning-based monitoring system for assessing the quality of cornea images captured by smartphones
evidence.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of image quality checks in flagging low-quality smartphone cornea images and their causes
evidence.effect: AUCs ranged from 0.984 to 0.999 across validation, internal, and external testing sets.
evidence.quote: This system performs well across validation, internal, and external testing sets, with AUCs ranging from 0.984 to 0.999.

evidence.title: Smartphone Imaging for Remote Monitoring of Inflammatory Arthritis in a Real-World Cohort: Longitudinal Evaluation of a Machine Learning-Based Finger Fold Biomarker
evidence.outcome: Proportion of images and joints unusable by the FFI algorithm because of input quality
evidence.effect: 78.3% of patient-acquired and 73.5% of HCP-acquired images were suitable to run the ML model; 23.1% of cropped joints were removed after the algorithm ran because of false detection.
evidence.quote: 23.1% of the cropped joints had to be removed after the running of the FFI algorithm due to false diameter or finger fold detection e.g. due to wrong hand positioning.

evidence.title: [The Digital Lab: Practical digital workflow and integration of AI for routine in pathology, through the example of prostate cancer]
evidence.outcome: Rate of AI analysis failures caused by poor-quality inputs (pre-analytical artifacts)
evidence.effect: A 10% failure rate related to pre-analytical artifacts was observed in routine use of the prostate AI tool.
evidence.quote: A 10% failure rate related to pre-analytical artifacts was observed and is an area for improvement in our practices.

evidence.title: Human Factors Validation Study of an Artificial Neural Network‑based Preoperative Decision‑support Tool for Noninvasive Lymph Node Staging (NILS) in Women with Primary Breast Cancer (ISRCTN99301435)
evidence.outcome: Whether the tool blocks invalid inputs (age, tumor size)
evidence.effect: Users could enter values outside valid ranges for age and tumor size, so the tool lacked input range checks.
evidence.quote: Several interface challenges were identified, including difficulty in locating the reset and information buttons, the ability to enter values outside valid ranges (age and tumor size), and the risk of unintentionally modifying the entered values while scrolling.

evidence.title: Impact of Imaging Protocols on Convolutional Neural Network-Based Pressure Injury Detection
evidence.outcome: Input protocol sensitivity
evidence.effect: Optical performance varied substantially across imaging protocols, 32-55% accuracy, indicating protocol-dependent reliability.
evidence.quote: In contrast, optical performance varied substantially across protocols (32-55% accuracy), demonstrating significant protocol dependency that could impact clinical implementation.

evidence.quote: Most discrepancies arose from incomplete or ambiguous documentation rather than model reasoning errors.

evidence.quote: At 4.5 m from the consultation, for all microphones tested, all facts were omitted.

evidence.effect: When crucial information was missing, average error rate was 45% for 20 cases, indicating unreliable outputs with incomplete inputs.
evidence.quote: The accuracy of ChatGPT decreased with increasing complexity; for example, in a variation where crucial information was missing, the AER was 45% for 20 cases.

evidence.effect: With Sparsified training, missing MRI sequences did not statistically affect performance; nn-Unet gave accurate segmentations despite incomplete MRI datasets.
evidence.quote: By applying Sparsified training, missing MRI sequences did not statistically affect the performance.

evidence.effect: LLM may overestimate frailty when less ADL information is provided.
evidence.quote: The LLM may overestimate frailty scores when less information about ADLs is provided, possibly as it is less subject to implicit assumptions and extrapolation than humans.

evidence.quote: This, along with the significant performance gains observed when providing case summaries instead of original medical reports, suggests that input data representation is the most critical factor in LLM performance.

evidence.quote: The AI did not identify the missing menopausal status as a critical variable.

evidence.quote: By comparing the performance of models on datasets with varying error rates (evaluated in terms of ROC-AUC), we observed that models were relatively tolerant to smaller error rates (<10%) but their performance significantly deteriorated at higher error rates (≥10%).

evidence.title: Effects of Image Degradation on Deep Neural Network Classification of Scaphoid Fracture Radiographs: Comparison Study of Different Noise Types

evidence.title: Evaluation Framework for Bruise Detection: Systematic ALS/White-Light Training and Skin-Tone Balancing with Deep Learning

evidence.title: A Reproducible Protocol and Framework for Large Language Model (LLM)-Assisted Estrogen and Progesterone Receptor (ER/PR) Scoring

evidence.title: Accuracy and Safety of Large Language Models in Endometrial Cancer Decision Making: A Case-Based In Silico Benchmarking Study
evidence.outcome: Recognition of missing decisive information in vignettes

commentary.bottom_line: Eleven studies test input quality checks, and most report that detectors flag poor-quality or incomplete inputs, with AUCs up to 0.77 in one study and as high as 0.999 in another, but all are offline or benchmark evaluations and one found no gain from gating. No study measured whether notifying users during live care changes clinical decisions or patient outcomes.

perspectives.view: All 11 tests are level 4 or 5 offline or benchmark studies. Reported AUCs were 0.933 to 0.995 for infant fundus images, 0.984 to 0.999 for smartphone cornea images, up to 0.77 for OCT scans, and 0.80 for anomalous documents. One study found that gating out poor images did not improve performance. Indirectness and inconsistency lower certainty to very low.

Hazard studies show that failures can pass silently. LLMs erred in 45% of neurology cases missing key information and hallucinated in 50 to 82.7% of cases after one fabricated detail. Filtering retinal images raised gene prediction accuracy from 33.8% to 68.9%, which suggests gating may prevent some errors, though no test tracked harm reaching patients.

In a replay of 28,185 visits, a confidence gate released forecasts at 32.7% to 48.1% of visits, and 51.5% of suppressions came from incomplete assessments rather than model uncertainty (0.2%). Input checks may therefore withhold output often. Clarification prompts improved LLM accuracy in automated benchmarks, and no study tested them in clinical workflows.

In routine use, a prostate AI tool failed on 10% of cases because of pre-analytical artifacts, and 21.7% to 26.5% of joint images were unsuitable for another algorithm. These figures suggest input checks will return a measurable share of cases to staff for rework or manual review, a cost that no testing study quantified.

Only one test involved non-English material. It used Japanese safety reports translated to English, and anomaly detection reached an AUROC of 0.80 with three counterexamples. A hazard study of German records traced most model discrepancies to incomplete documentation. No test reported Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy populations.

FDA draft guidance asks developers to list compatible devices and acceptable acquisition protocols, and FUTURE-AI and CHAI frameworks call for mechanisms that identify erroneous or missing inputs. All four sources use should-level language. No study tested whether specifying protocols in device labeling reduces use with incompatible inputs.

In one vignette study, GPT-4o asked for missing acne medication details and OpenBioLLM-70B did not. In another, models failed to detect ambiguity in weekday-phrased patient questions. Patients may receive advice built on incomplete information without knowing it, and no study examined whether patients understood or acted on input-quality notices.

commentary.research_gap: No study deployed input quality checks with user notification in live clinical care and compared error rates, clinician responses, workload, or patient outcomes against a setting without checks. Studies are also needed that test whether published protocol specifications hold across device vendors and how often clinicians override or ignore quality notifications.
commentary.underserved_note: One test used Japanese safety reports that had been translated to English, but these were regulatory case reports and did not involve patients with limited English proficiency. No test included Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy populations, so the performance of input checks on records and images from those settings remains unknown.
